mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, no significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold upward.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as expectations of future rate cuts boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: In 20 out of 60 windows where the trigger occurs, forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in PAYEMS (labor market strength) of over 2% in a month is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as investors anticipate higher inflation and tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% in a month
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, less than 40% produce negative 5-day forward returns (proportion > 60%).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (goods demand) grows faster than CPIAUCSL (price index) for two consecutive quarters, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 20-day forward return as demand growth outpaces price inflation.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth rate > CPIAUCSL quarterly growth rate for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: In 50 such triggered windows, the 20-day return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 3% while HOUST (retail sales) remains flat suggests supply-side strength, which predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to profit margin compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >3% while HOUST is flat in the same month
failure_condition: More than 40% of such events result in non-negative 20-day returns (proportion < 60%).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as labor market weakness is interpreted as a recovery signal.
failure_condition: Across 30 such windows, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (reserves) of over 10% in a month combined with a decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% suggests deflationary pressure, which should drive a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% in a month AND CPIAUCSL < 2%
failure_condition: In 80% of such events, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (proportion > 20%).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where PAYEMS (employment) grows by at least 4% month-over-month for three months, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to expectations of wage-price spirals and tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >=4% each month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 50 such periods, less than 30% produce negative 5-day returns (proportion > 70%).
